blocks.text: Iguazú Falls and a rainbow over the river, surrounded by tropical forest in Brazil
Iguazú Falls in Brazil: cascades, a rainbow and green riverbanks
The Argentine Side of Iguazú Falls

After breakfast, leave early for Iguazú National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

Ride the park’s eco-train through dense forest, then follow footpaths and walkways beside the falls. There are 3 main sections: the Lower Circuit, the Upper Circuit and the Devil’s Throat. Each takes you to a different height relative to the water, giving you a different view of the same system of cascades.

**Lower Circuit:** Around 1,700 metres of footpaths pass below the main cascades, letting you see them from underneath. The route takes in the Álvar Núñez, Elenita and Lanusse falls, as well as Salto Bossetti, which drops in a broad sheet of water. Allow around 1 hour and 45 minutes. The route is moderately challenging.

**Upper Circuit:** The route is around 1,300 metres long. The paths run near the top of the cascades, so you can watch the water reach the edge and plunge below. The Adam and Eve falls are among the best-known on this route. Allow around 1 hour. The route is easy and has no stairs.

**Devil’s Throat:** The water plunges around 82 metres, and you can hear it long before you reach the viewing platform. Take the eco-train again to reach the start of the trail, then follow the walkways to the most powerful cascade.

After the tour, transfer to your hotel. You’ll have seen the falls from 3 distinct perspectives: from below, from the top edge and beside the most powerful cascade. Together, these views give you a close look at Iguazú from the Argentine side.
